items.title: Added PowerShell tool for Windows as an opt-in preview. Learn more at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#powershell-tool

explanation.what_it_is: The PowerShell tool is a new opt-in preview feature for Windows users, allowing them to utilize PowerShell within Claude Code.
explanation.why_it_matters: This addition enables Windows users to leverage PowerShell's capabilities, such as automating tasks and executing scripts, directly within Claude Code.
how_to_use: Opt-in to the PowerShell tool preview through the Claude Code settings
Use the PowerShell tool to run scripts and automate tasks on Windows
Refer to the tools reference documentation at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#powershell-tool for more information

items.title: Added ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL_SUPPORTS env vars to override effort/thinking capability detection for pinned default models for 3p…

explanation.what_it_is: The ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL_SUPPORTS environment variables allow you to override the default effort and thinking capability detection for pinned models.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more control over model behavior, particularly when working with third-party models, by enabling them to manually specify the capabilities of their default models.
how_to_use: Set ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_SUPPORTS to override the default OPUS model capabilities
Set ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL_SUPPORTS to override the default SONNET model capabilities
Set ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL_SUPPORTS to override the default HAIKU model capabilities

items.title: Added CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS env var to configure the streaming idle watchdog threshold (default 90s)

explanation.what_it_is: The CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable allows you to configure the threshold for the streaming idle watchdog, which determines how long a stream can be idle before it is considered inactive.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more control over the streaming idle timeout, allowing them to adjust the threshold to suit their specific use cases and avoid unnecessary stream closures.
how_to_use: Set CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS to a higher value (e.g., 300000) to increase the idle timeout for long-running streams
Set CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS to a lower value (e.g., 30000) to decrease the idle timeout for streams that require more frequent activity

items.title: Added TaskCreated hook that fires when a task is created via TaskCreate

explanation.what_it_is: The TaskCreated hook is a new event trigger in Claude Code that activates when a task is created using the TaskCreate function.
explanation.why_it_matters: This hook allows developers to execute custom code or workflows immediately after a new task is created, enabling automated reactions to task creation events.
how_to_use: Use the TaskCreated hook to send notifications to team members when a new task is assigned to them.
Implement custom logging or analytics when tasks are created to track project activity.

items.title: Added WorktreeCreate hook support for type: "http" — return the created worktree path via hookSpecificOutput.worktreePath in the response JSON

explanation.what_it_is: The WorktreeCreate hook now supports type 'http', allowing you to create a worktree and receive the created worktree path in the response JSON.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to automate worktree creation over HTTP and retrieve the created worktree path for further processing or integration with other tools.
how_to_use: Use the WorktreeCreate hook with type 'http' to create a worktree and retrieve the created path
Access the created worktree path via the hookSpecificOutput.worktreePath field in the response JSON

items.title: Added allowedChannelPlugins managed setting for team/enterprise admins to define a channel plugin allowlist

explanation.what_it_is: The allowedChannelPlugins managed setting allows team and enterprise admins to define a list of approved channel plugins that can be used within their organization.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives admins control over which channel plugins are allowed, enabling them to enforce security and compliance policies within their team or enterprise.
how_to_use: Define a list of approved channel plugins in the allowedChannelPlugins setting
Use this setting to restrict access to specific plugins for security or compliance reasons

items.title: Added x-client-request-id header to API requests for debugging timeouts

explanation.what_it_is: The x-client-request-id header is now included in API requests made by Claude Code, providing a unique identifier for each request.
explanation.why_it_matters: This addition facilitates debugging of timeouts by allowing users to track and identify specific requests that are timing out.
how_to_use: Include the x-client-request-id header in API request logs to correlate requests with timeout errors
Use the x-client-request-id to identify and retry failed requests

items.title: Added idle-return prompt that nudges users returning after 75+ minutes to /clear, reducing unnecessary token re-caching on stale sessions

explanation.what_it_is: A prompt that appears when a user returns to Claude Code after 75+ minutes of inactivity, suggesting they run the /clear command to reset their session.
explanation.why_it_matters: This reduces unnecessary token re-caching on stale sessions, which can help prevent issues with outdated session data.
how_to_use: When prompted, run the /clear command to reset your session and avoid potential issues with stale data.
Use this prompt as a reminder to regularly clear your session when working with sensitive or frequently updated data.

items.title: [VSCode] Added rate limit warning banner with usage percentage and reset time

explanation.what_it_is: A rate limit warning banner in VSCode that displays the current usage percentage and reset time.
explanation.why_it_matters: This banner helps Claude Code users in VSCode track their rate limit usage and plan accordingly to avoid hitting the limit, reducing the likelihood of interrupted workflows.
how_to_use: Monitor the banner to stay aware of your current usage percentage
Plan your tasks around the reset time to minimize disruptions

items.title: Added managed-settings.d/ drop-in directory alongside managed-settings.json, letting separate teams deploy independent policy fragments that merge…

explanation.what_it_is: A new drop-in directory called managed-settings.d/ that allows separate teams to deploy independent policy fragments, which merge with the existing managed-settings.json file.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables multiple teams to manage their own policy settings independently, without having to coordinate changes to a single file, making it easier to manage complex configurations.
how_to_use: Create a new file in the managed-settings.d/ directory to define a policy fragment specific to your team
Use this file to override or extend settings defined in the main managed-settings.json file

items.title: Added CwdChanged and FileChanged hook events for reactive environment management (e.g., direnv)

explanation.what_it_is: The CwdChanged and FileChanged hook events allow Claude Code to detect changes in the current working directory and file system, enabling reactive environment management.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to automate tasks and manage their environment in response to changes in the file system, such as when using direnv.
how_to_use: Use the CwdChanged event to trigger actions when the current working directory changes
Use the FileChanged event to trigger actions when a file is modified or updated

items.title: Added sandbox.failIfUnavailable setting to exit with an error when sandbox is enabled but cannot start, instead of running unsandboxed

explanation.what_it_is: The sandbox.failIfUnavailable setting allows Claude Code to exit with an error when the sandbox is enabled but cannot start, preventing the application from running unsandboxed.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting ensures that Claude Code maintains its sandboxed environment, preventing potential security risks when the sandbox cannot be initialized.
how_to_use: Set sandbox.failIfUnavailable to true in your configuration to enable this behavior
Use this setting in environments where sandboxing is required for security or compliance reasons

items.title: Added disableDeepLinkRegistration setting to prevent claude-cli:// protocol handler registration

explanation.what_it_is: The disableDeepLinkRegistration setting prevents the registration of the claude-cli:// protocol handler, which is used to handle deep links in Claude Code.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives users control over whether Claude Code registers the protocol handler, which can be useful in environments where such registrations are not desired or are restricted.
how_to_use: Set disableDeepLinkRegistration to true in your configuration to prevent the claude-cli:// protocol handler from being registered.
Use this setting on platforms where protocol handler registration is not allowed or is unwanted.

items.title: Added CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 to strip Anthropic and cloud provider credentials from subprocess environments (Bash tool, hooks, MCP stdio…

explanation.what_it_is: A new environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 that removes Anthropic and cloud provider credentials from subprocess environments in Claude Code.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update helps prevent accidental exposure of sensitive credentials when running subprocesses, such as Bash tools or hooks, in Claude Code.
how_to_use: Set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1 in your environment to enable credential stripping for subprocesses.
Use this variable in conjunction with Bash tools or hooks to ensure credentials are removed from subprocess environments.

items.title: Added transcript search — press / in transcript mode (Ctrl+O) to search, n/N to step through matches

explanation.what_it_is: Transcript search allows you to find specific text within a transcript by pressing / in transcript mode, with Ctrl+O as a shortcut. This enables a search function within the transcript.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update streamlines the process of locating specific parts of a transcript, saving time for Claude Code users who need to review or reference particular sections. It simplifies navigation within transcripts.
how_to_use: Press / in transcript mode to initiate a search
Use Ctrl+O as a shortcut to start searching
Press n/N to step through search matches

items.title: Added Ctrl+X Ctrl+E as an alias for opening the external editor (readline-native binding; Ctrl+G still works)

explanation.what_it_is: A new keyboard shortcut, Ctrl+X Ctrl+E, that opens the external editor in Claude Code, in addition to the existing Ctrl+G shortcut.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update provides an alternative way to access the external editor, which may be more familiar or convenient for some users, particularly those accustomed to readline-native bindings.
how_to_use: Press Ctrl+X Ctrl+E to open the external editor from within Claude Code
Use Ctrl+G as an alternative shortcut to achieve the same result

items.title: Deprecated TaskOutput tool in favor of using Read on the background task's output file path

explanation.what_it_is: The TaskOutput tool has been deprecated, and users are now expected to use the Read function to access the output file path of a background task.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change requires users to update their workflows to use the Read function, which provides a more direct way to access task output.
how_to_use: Replace TaskOutput with Read('/path/to/background/task/output') in your code
Update your task output handling to use the Read function's file path parameter

items.title: Added --bare flag for scripted -p calls — skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync, and skill directory walks; requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper via…

explanation.what_it_is: The --bare flag is a new option for scripted -p calls in Claude Code, which skips certain features like hooks, LSP, plugin sync, and skill directory walks to simplify the process.
explanation.why_it_matters: This flag matters because it allows for faster and more lightweight scripted calls, which can be useful for automation or testing purposes, and it requires either an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper for authentication.
how_to_use: Use the --bare flag with a scripted -p call to bypass unnecessary features and speed up the process, for example: `claude-code -p --bare`
Make sure to set an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or use an apiKeyHelper to authenticate your scripted calls when using the --bare flag

items.title: Added --channels permission relay — channel servers that declare the permission capability can forward tool approval prompts to your phone

explanation.what_it_is: The --channels permission relay allows channel servers to forward tool approval prompts to your phone, if they declare the permission capability.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables more flexible approval workflows, as users can now receive and respond to prompts on their phone instead of being tied to their computer.
how_to_use: Run Claude Code with the --channels flag to enable permission relay
Configure your channel server to declare the permission capability

items.title: Added rate_limits field to statusline scripts for displaying Claude.ai rate limit usage (5-hour and 7-day windows with used_percentage and resets_at)

explanation.what_it_is: The rate_limits field is a new addition to statusline scripts, allowing users to display their Claude.ai rate limit usage. It provides data for 5-hour and 7-day windows, including used_percentage and resets_at.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to monitor their rate limit usage directly within their statusline scripts, helping them avoid unexpected rate limit errors. It provides more transparency into their API usage.
how_to_use: Access the rate_limits field in your statusline script to display current rate limit usage
Use the used_percentage value to create custom warnings when approaching rate limits
Utilize the resets_at value to schedule tasks around rate limit resets

items.title: Added source: 'settings' plugin marketplace source — declare plugin entries inline in settings.json

explanation.what_it_is: The 'settings' plugin marketplace source allows declaring plugin entries directly in the settings.json file, streamlining plugin management.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update simplifies plugin configuration by eliminating the need for separate plugin configuration files, making it easier to manage and track plugin entries in a single location.
how_to_use: Declare a plugin entry in settings.json by adding a 'plugins' section with the plugin name and version
Use the 'settings' source to manage plugin dependencies and updates from the plugin marketplace

items.title: Added CLI tool usage detection to plugin tips, in addition to file pattern matching

explanation.what_it_is: The Claude Code plugin now detects CLI tool usage in addition to file pattern matching to provide more accurate tips.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code to offer more relevant suggestions based on the tools being used, potentially reducing the time spent searching for the right commands or configurations.
how_to_use: Run a CLI tool in your project to see tool-specific tips in the Claude Code plugin
Use file pattern matching in conjunction with CLI tool detection for more precise plugin suggestions

items.title: Added effort frontmatter support for skills and slash commands to override the model effort level when invoked

explanation.what_it_is: Effort frontmatter support allows you to specify a custom effort level for skills and slash commands, overriding the default model effort level when invoked.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more control over the effort level applied to specific skills and commands, enabling more fine-grained customization of model behavior.
how_to_use: Add effort frontmatter to a skill to override the default effort level for that skill
Use effort frontmatter with a slash command to customize the effort level for a specific command invocation

items.title: Added --channels (research preview) — allow MCP servers to push messages into your session

explanation.what_it_is: The --channels option allows MCP servers to push messages directly into your Claude Code session, enabling real-time communication.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature enables MCP servers to proactively send messages to users, changing how users interact with these servers in their Claude Code workflow.
how_to_use: Use the --channels option when connecting to an MCP server to enable push messages
Test the --channels option in a research preview environment to explore its capabilities

items.title: Added --console flag to claude auth login for Anthropic Console (API billing) authentication

explanation.what_it_is: The --console flag is a new option for the claude auth login command, specifically for Anthropic Console API billing authentication.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to authenticate with Anthropic Console using the API billing method, which may be required for certain workflows or billing setups.
how_to_use: Use the --console flag with claude auth login to authenticate with Anthropic Console API billing
Example: claude auth login --console

items.title: Added "Show turn duration" toggle to the /config menu

explanation.what_it_is: A toggle in the /config menu that controls the display of turn duration in Claude Code.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature allows users to customize their workflow by choosing whether or not to see turn duration, which can be useful for optimizing conversation flows.
how_to_use: Go to the /config menu and toggle 'Show turn duration' to enable or disable the feature.
Use this toggle to hide turn duration when it's not relevant to your current task, reducing visual clutter.

items.title: [VSCode] Added /remote-control — bridge your session to claude.ai/code to continue from a browser or phone

explanation.what_it_is: The /remote-control command allows you to bridge your current VSCode session to claude.ai/code, enabling continuation of work from a browser or phone.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature matters because it provides flexibility in workflow, allowing Claude Code users to switch between devices and environments seamlessly.
how_to_use: Run the /remote-control command in VSCode to initiate the bridging process
Access your bridged session from a browser by visiting claude.ai/code
Use your phone's browser to continue working on your session from anywhere

items.title: We've added model capability fields to the Models API
items.summary: We've added model capability fields to the Models API. GET /v1/models and GET /v1/models/{model_id} now return max_input_tokens, max_tokens, and a capabilities object. Query the API to discover what…

explanation.what_it_is: The Models API now includes model capability fields, which provide information about the limitations and features of each model, such as max_input_tokens, max_tokens, and a capabilities object.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update allows Claude Code users to programmatically discover the capabilities of each model, enabling more informed decisions when selecting models for specific tasks.
how_to_use: Use the GET /v1/models endpoint to retrieve a list of models with their corresponding capabilities
Query the GET /v1/models/{model_id} endpoint to get the capabilities of a specific model
Check the capabilities object to determine the supported features and limitations of a model before using it

items.title: Added StopFailure hook event that fires when the turn ends due to an API error (rate limit, auth failure, etc.)

explanation.what_it_is: The StopFailure hook event is a new event in Claude Code that triggers when a turn ends due to an API error, such as rate limiting or authentication failure.
explanation.why_it_matters: This event allows developers to handle and respond to API errors in a more explicit way, enabling better error handling and debugging in their applications.
how_to_use: Use the StopFailure hook to log API error events for debugging purposes
Implement retry logic in response to StopFailure events to handle transient API errors

items.title: Added ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} variable for plugin persistent state that survives plugin updates; /plugin uninstall prompts before deleting it

explanation.what_it_is: The ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} variable allows plugins to store persistent state that remains intact even after plugin updates. This variable enables plugins to retain data across different versions.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update changes how plugins manage data, allowing them to maintain consistency and avoid data loss after updates. It also introduces a prompt before uninstalling a plugin to prevent accidental data deletion.
how_to_use: Use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} to store plugin settings or user preferences that should persist across updates
Access the stored data in your plugin to provide a consistent user experience
Confirm or cancel the uninstallation of a plugin when prompted to avoid unintentionally deleting persistent data

items.title: Added effort, maxTurns, and disallowedTools frontmatter support for plugin-shipped agents

explanation.what_it_is: The effort, maxTurns, and disallowedTools frontmatter options are now supported for agents shipped with plugins, allowing for more fine-grained control over agent behavior.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives developers more flexibility in configuring plugin-shipped agents, enabling them to tailor agent behavior to specific use cases.
how_to_use: Add effort, maxTurns, and disallowedTools options to an agent's frontmatter to customize its behavior
Use these options to limit the number of turns an agent can take or restrict the tools it can use

items.title: Added ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION env var to add a custom entry to the /model picker, with optional _NAME and _DESCRIPTION suffixed vars for display

explanation.what_it_is: The ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION environment variable allows you to add a custom model to the model picker in Claude Code. You can also specify a custom name and description for the model using the _NAME and _DESCRIPTION suffixed variables.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more flexibility in managing their models, allowing them to easily add and identify custom models. It simplifies the workflow for users who need to work with multiple custom models.
how_to_use: Set the ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION environment variable to the path of your custom model
Optionally, set ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_NAME and ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_DESCRIPTION to customize the display name and description of your model

items.title: Added allowRead sandbox filesystem setting to re-allow read access within denyRead regions

explanation.what_it_is: The allowRead sandbox filesystem setting allows read access to specific regions of the filesystem that were previously blocked by denyRead settings.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more fine-grained control over filesystem access, enabling read operations in areas where they were previously restricted.
how_to_use: Set allowRead to true in your sandbox filesystem configuration to override denyRead settings for specific regions.
Use this setting to enable read access to specific files or directories within a denyRead region.

items.title: We've launched the display field for extended thinking, letting you omit…
items.summary: We've launched the display field for extended thinking, letting you omit thinking content from responses for faster streaming. Set thinking.display: "omitted" to receive thinking blocks with an empty…

explanation.what_it_is: The display field for extended thinking allows you to control whether thinking content is included in responses, with the option to omit it for faster streaming.
explanation.why_it_matters: This change enables faster response times by excluding unnecessary thinking content, which can be beneficial for applications where speed is critical.
how_to_use: Set thinking.display: 'omitted' to receive thinking blocks with empty content
Use this feature to optimize streaming performance in applications with tight latency requirements

items.title: Added MCP elicitation support — MCP servers can now request structured input mid-task via an interactive dialog (form fields or browser URL)

explanation.what_it_is: MCP elicitation support allows MCP servers to request structured input from users mid-task through interactive dialogs, which can be filled out using form fields or by providing a browser URL.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables more dynamic and interactive tasks in Claude Code, as MCP servers can now collect specific information from users at any point during a task.
how_to_use: Use the MCP elicitation support to request user input for tasks that require dynamic data, such as filling out a form or providing a URL for further processing.
Implement interactive dialogs in your MCP servers to collect structured input from users and create more flexible workflows.

items.title: Added new Elicitation and ElicitationResult hooks to intercept and override responses before they're sent back

explanation.what_it_is: New hooks for Elicitation and ElicitationResult that allow interception and override of responses before they are sent back
explanation.why_it_matters: This update gives Claude Code users more control over the response pipeline, enabling custom modifications or filtering of responses
how_to_use: Use the Elicitation hook to modify input data before it's processed
Use the ElicitationResult hook to override or transform the response before it's returned to the user

items.title: Added -n / --name <name> CLI flag to set a display name for the session at startup

explanation.what_it_is: The -n or --name CLI flag allows you to specify a custom display name for your Claude Code session when starting up from the command line.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature enables you to easily identify and distinguish between multiple Claude Code sessions running concurrently, making it simpler to manage your workflow.
how_to_use: Use the flag by appending -n or --name followed by your desired session name, e.g., `claude-code -n my_session`
Replace `my_session` with any name that helps you identify the purpose or context of the session

items.title: Added worktree.sparsePaths setting for claude --worktree in large monorepos to check out only the directories you need via git sparse-checkout

explanation.what_it_is: The worktree.sparsePaths setting allows you to specify directories to check out when using claude --worktree in large monorepos, utilizing git sparse-checkout to only retrieve necessary files.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting helps reduce the amount of data that needs to be checked out, making it faster and more efficient to work with large monorepos.
how_to_use: Use the worktree.sparsePaths setting to specify directories to check out, such as 'claude --worktree --sparse-paths=dir1,dir2'
Configure git sparse-checkout to only retrieve necessary files, reducing the amount of data that needs to be checked out

items.title: Added PostCompact hook that fires after compaction completes

explanation.what_it_is: The PostCompact hook is a new event that triggers after the compaction process is complete, allowing for custom actions to be taken after data has been compacted.
explanation.why_it_matters: This hook enables Claude Code users to automate tasks or run custom scripts immediately after compaction, streamlining their workflow and reducing manual intervention.
how_to_use: Use the PostCompact hook to send a notification when compaction is complete
Run a custom script to analyze compacted data
Trigger a data export after compaction

items.title: Added /effort slash command to set model effort level

explanation.what_it_is: The /effort slash command allows you to set the model effort level, controlling the trade-off between response speed and accuracy.
explanation.why_it_matters: This command gives Claude Code users more control over the model's behavior, enabling them to adjust the effort level based on their specific needs and priorities.
how_to_use: Use /effort low to prioritize speed for simple queries
Use /effort medium for a balance between speed and accuracy
Use /effort high for complex queries that require more accurate responses

items.title: Added session quality survey — enterprise admins can configure the sample rate via the feedbackSurveyRate setting

explanation.what_it_is: A session quality survey that collects feedback from users, with a configurable sample rate set by enterprise admins via the feedbackSurveyRate setting.
explanation.why_it_matters: This feature allows enterprise admins to gather targeted feedback from users, helping to identify and improve the quality of sessions in Claude Code.
how_to_use: Set the feedbackSurveyRate to a specific percentage, such as 10%, to control how often users are prompted to take the survey.
Use the survey feedback to inform improvements to session quality, such as adjusting settings or optimizing workflows.

items.title: Added actionable suggestions to /context command — identifies context-heavy tools, memory bloat, and capacity warnings with specific optimization tips

explanation.what_it_is: The /context command now provides actionable suggestions to help optimize context-heavy tools, memory bloat, and capacity warnings.
explanation.why_it_matters: This update enables Claude Code users to identify and address performance issues more efficiently, with specific tips for optimization.
how_to_use: Run the /context command to receive suggestions for optimizing context-heavy tools
Use the command to identify memory bloat and receive tips for reducing it
Address capacity warnings with specific optimization recommendations

items.title: Added autoMemoryDirectory setting to configure a custom directory for auto-memory storage

explanation.what_it_is: The autoMemoryDirectory setting allows you to specify a custom directory for storing auto-memory data in Claude Code.
explanation.why_it_matters: This setting gives you control over where auto-memory data is stored, which can be useful for managing disk space or organizing project files.
how_to_use: Set autoMemoryDirectory to a custom path in your project settings to store auto-memory data outside the default directory.
Use this setting to keep auto-memory data separate from other project files for easier cleanup or archiving.
